 Game devs still want to develop and optimize for Steam Deck and Nintendo Switch, survey suggests
 Handheld form factors remain an important 
 Jack Goodall Staff Writer 
 Last Updated on November 17, 2026 
 Follow us
 Add us on

 Table of Contents 
 Latest tech deals. 
 Switch 2, Steam Deck, and Steam Machine are more popular than Xbox 
 GDC’s annual State of the Game Industry report has been published, with some of the biggest topics of discussion being the large number of (mass) layoffs this year , the recurring issue of generative AI, project funding, and much more. The report also provides us with nuggets of information in the form of game developer surveys. Unsurprisingly, more than 80% of devs say they are interested in developing for PC, and a smaller percentage for Valve’s Linux-based Steam Deck and Steam Machine systems.
 🔥 More offers: see our Steam Deck Black Friday deals 2026 guide, updated daily, or browse all Black Friday deals .
 The original Switch may be falling down the popularity chart, but the Nintendo Switch 2 is replacing it as a major platform devs want to develop for, according to the recent survey. It ranks even higher than the PlayStation 5, and it’s far above the Xbox Series X|S. Despite the extra considerations and optimizations required for handheld systems such as the Deck and Switch 2, devs remain interested.

 Switch 2, Steam Deck, and Steam Machine are more popular than Xbox
 While it will be nearly impossible to dethrone PC, it’s interesting to see that nearly half (46%) of those surveyed are interested in developing for the Nintendo Switch 2. It’s the newest console from the big three, and the 29% vote for the Steam Machine, released at the end of June, is a notable inclusion, though you could argue it can also fall under the PC category, certainly if Valve’s Proton compatibility layer can handle some of the technical side, especially from a small indie developer’s perspective.

 We’ve seen developers in the past championing Steam Deck support , and a shiny green ‘Verified’ badge is a great way of attracting handheld players. Valve has rolled out a similar compatibility system for the Steam Machine and Steam Frame, and even more recently, Steam Deck users gained access to performance benchmarks built directly into the Steam store .
 It’s important to point out that the survey gauges developers’ interest more than anything. A separate graph shows a revealing split between free-to-play and premium titles per platform. Both the Steam Deck and Nintendo Switch 2 fall off in the free-to-play space, where Android climbs the ranks to 58%, just behind PC at 61%, marking a 7% reduction for the latter compared to GDC’s previous survey.
 Earlier this year, another GDC report told us that less than a third of game developers (28%) actually test their games on Steam Deck, though a higher percentage (40%) do wish to better support it. Since then, Valve has launched the Steam Machine and Steam Frame, both of which run on SteamOS, giving developers even more excuse to optimize for the Linux-based operating system.
